jess_support: Hi @michael_acme — thanks for the report. I see you're seeing inconsistent cache hits for embeddings when you include a customer-specific prefix in your requests. Can you paste an example request body (no secrets)? :wave:

michael_acme: yeah, here's a redacted one. we call /v1/embeddings with body: 
```json
{
  "model": "text-embedding-ada-002",
  "input": "order-12345: The user message...",
  "tenant_id": "acme-corp"
}
```
Sometimes we get cache hits (fast, 40ms) and sometimes full recompute (~450ms) for the same input. Billing spikes too. Not sure why.

acme_integration_bot: NOTE: request_id=r-0f3b2a; route=embedding.compute; model_variant=ada-v2; key_prefix=order-12345; cache_lookup=attempted

jess_support: thanks. A few clarifying q's: 1) Are you consistently including the same prefix formatting (e.g., `order-12345:`) and spacing? 2) Are you batching those calls? 3) Any chance different pipeline components change or normalize the prefix?

michael_acme: 1) yes it's consistent from our side. 2) we batch up to 8 inputs per request sometimes. 3) we have a small proxy that adds `tenant_id` header and also normalizes whitespace, but we don't touch the `input` string.

sanjay_eng_ml: looping in eng-ml. Two hypotheses: 1) prefix is being used as part of cache key but there's a TTL or sharding by GPU pool that causes misses; 2) batching changes canonicalization of strings (we dedupe and canonicalize keys per-batch). I'll try to reproduce. Can you share a couple of raw batched payloads (timestamps ok)?

michael_acme: posted two samples to the secure link. Sample A: single input with prefix. Sample B: batch of 6 with same prefix repeated in each input. In the batch case we saw more misses.

jess_support: copying logs around the times you saw misses...

deploybot: Deploy succeeded: routing-change v3 -> v4 at 2026-03-12T16:09:03Z (no rolling restarts).

acme_integration_bot: CACHE: hit=false key=tenant:acme-corp|model:ada-v2|digest:7a9c3 TTL=3600 shard=pool-12

acme_integration_bot: CACHE: hit=true key=tenant:acme-corp|model:ada-v2|digest:7a9c3 TTL=3594 shard=pool-07

jess_support: these log lines are interesting — same digest but different shard. That suggests the same input hashed the same (digest) but looked up in different cache shard/pool. If there's per-pool caching (not global), then routing differences can cause apparent inconsistent hits. @sanjay_eng_ml, do we route by pool based on capacity and does cache populate across pools?

sanjay_eng_ml: Good catch. We route by policy (latency and capacity) and there's a per-pool LRU cache for embeddings. Cache fill is per-shard, no global invalidation propagation. Normally requests for the same tenant/model will prefer the same pool via affinity, but we recently added burst/overflow to move requests to other pools when latency spikes — that can cause transient misses.

michael_acme: ah — that would explain hit vs miss. But why does the digest match across misses/hits? I assume digest is just input hashing, independent of shard.

sanjay_eng_ml: exactly — digest = sha256(input+model+prefixKey) computed client-side in our proxy. The cache key also includes tenant and model but the lookup is scoped to a pool. So the digest can be same but lookup misses if you're routed elsewhere. Two fixes: 1) make key have global namespace or 2) ensure stronger routing affinity for tenant prefixes. Both have tradeoffs.

jess_support: follow-up: you mentioned batching increases misses. Reason: during batch processing we canonicalize and dedupe inputs within the batch, and then we attempt to fetch per-shard. If a batch is split across pools (due to concurrency) dedupe may be less effective. Also prefix normalization differences (trailing spaces) between inputs can cause different digests.

michael_acme: we do see sometimes trailing whitespace appended by our logging middleware for some items. Could that flip digest?

sanjay_eng_ml: yes, even a single extra space changes sha256. For repro try exact strings. Quick repro steps I used: 
1) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer x" -d '{"model":"ada-v2","input":"order-12345: hello","tenant_id":"acme-corp"}' 
2) repeat 10x rapidly -> should hit same shard if affinity holds. 
3) then send a 6-item batch with same strings concurrently from a different client -> observe which pool handles it.

acme_integration_bot: DEBUG: batch-id=bd-77; routing=spread; candidates=[pool-07,pool-12]; decision=spread-to-fit

jess_support: To rule out a dimension mismatch/batching interplay: one customer previously had an embeddings shape mismatch when passing arrays vs single strings. Make sure you are sending single strings as expected by the model. If you send precomputed vector arrays by mistake cache logic will skip (and billing looks different).

michael_acme: we are sending strings. No precomputed vectors. Confirmed.

olivia_billing: chiming in on billing spikes: when cache misses we bill full token compute. If the same digest is computed multiple times across different pools, you'll see duplicate compute charges. We can run a billing audit for suspect windows. If you want immediate relief, consider lowering per-request concurrency or enabling tenant-affinity pinning for a short window (we can do that via support).

jess_support: Action items for short term:
- @michael_acme: try disabling your proxy's whitespace normalization or strip trailing spaces consistently, then retest single vs batched calls.
- @sanjay_eng_ml: can we enable tenant-affinity pinning for acme-corp for 24h and see hit rate?
- @olivia_billing: please flag the window 2026-03-12T15:50 -> 2026-03-12T17:00 for audit.

sanjay_eng_ml: I can enable affinity pinning for tenant=acme-corp to prefer pool-07 where most of their cache exists. Will monitor hit rate and revert after 24h.

michael_acme: trying a quick test now. Sending single requests 20x then a batch of 6. Will post timings.

acme_integration_bot: TIMING: single-run avg=42ms (15 hits, 5 misses) batch-run avg=368ms (2 hits, 4 misses)

michael_acme: ok after enabling affinity pinning from sanjay we're seeing: single-run avg=38ms (19 hits, 1 miss) batch-run avg=62ms (5 hits, 1 miss). Huge difference. Thanks.

jess_support: great. Root cause summary: per-pool scoped embedding caches + routing/spread behavior + minor whitespace variance in inputs led to inconsistent cache behavior. Batched requests exacerbate the issue when routing splits inputs across pools.

jess_support: long-term ops notes (for eng): consider one or more of: global cache indexing (with async replication), more deterministic tenant->pool affinity, or include shard id in monitoring to make this easier to triage. Also document that input canonicalization (whitespace) affects client-side digest.

michael_acme: appreciate the quick help. Can you confirm we'll get a billing credit for the duplicate computes?

olivia_billing: we'll review and open a billing ticket. If the audit shows duplicate full computes directly caused by our routing change we can credit back a portion. I'll DM to get account details.

jess_support: closing the loop: I've added repro steps to the case, linked internal note with logs, and scheduled a 24h telemetry check. Posting concise TL;DR for your engineers: 
- Ensure exact canonicalization of input strings (trim spaces).
- Avoid mixing high-concurrency batched sends that may be routed differently.
- Request tenant-affinity pinning from support if you need deterministic cache locality.

michael_acme: TL;DR received. Thanks all :pray:

deploybot: Incident watch scheduled for tenant-affinity toggle (24h)

jess_support: marking case as monitoring. Reopen if you see regressions. :white_check_mark:
